group: B (provisional: GamesRadar names 4 developers; TENSTACK's LinkedIn credits 3 developers plus separate art, audio and marketing people, so total contributors may exceed 5)
title: Gamble With Your Friends
genre: Online co-op 'casino crawler' / friendslop: 1–6 players share one bank account and one massive debt, gamble through 16 casino games and climb a casino tower to meet a loan shark's quota within 5 minutes
developer: TEAM GWYF (Steam credit). GamesRadar/KitGuru name four developers by handle: SkyBrave, blazitt, Gevizz and Kiwick. A TENSTACK LinkedIn post names developers Yiğit Doruk, Doruk Sasmaz and Fatih Görgüç, plus art/audio/marketing contributors. Erik Levin de Verdier brought the team together under TENSTACK.
team_size: ~4 developers [CONFIRMED – GamesRadar/KitGuru]; plus art, audio and marketing contributors per TENSTACK LinkedIn, so the total is probably ~5–8 [ESTIMATE]
country: Sweden (described as a Swedish team; TENSTACK collective; at least one developer LinkedIn-located in Sweden). Individual nationalities not confirmed.
developer_background: Part of TENSTACK, 'a small collective of game makers creating lots of creative and digestible games'. The same label is behind/associated with Sledding Game (bundled together on Steam). Previous games by the individual developers: no data.
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (PC): https://store.steampowered.com/app/3892270/Gamble_With_Your_Friends/ ; Steam bundles with How to Fish and Sledding Game. Consoles: no data.
business_model: Premium $7.99, discounts seen at -20% ($6.39) and -38% ($4.95). No real-money gambling; cross-promotional bundles with other friendslop hits (How to Fish, Sledding Game).
price_usd: $7.99 list [CONFIRMED – Steam]; launch discount: no data (a -38% $4.95 price seen in a later snapshot)
units_or_downloads: 500,000 by 2026-05-04 (3 days) [CONFIRMED – devs via GamesRadar/KitGuru; WN Hub says May 5]; 600k→700k on ~2026-05-07 (Automaton: 'announcements can't keep up'); 1,000,000 by ~2026-05-08/09 (1 week) [CONFIRMED – TENSTACK via GosuGamers/Gamereactor]; 2,000,000 by ~2026-06-04 (1 month) [CONFIRMED – TENSTACK LinkedIn / WN Hub]. ~3.2M units by 2026-08-18 [ESTIMATE – VG Insights via SteamPulse].
peak_concurrent_players: All-time peak 42,488 in May 2026 [ESTIMATE – Raijin, checked 2026-10-07]; SteamCharts shows 24,666 (older or partial snapshot). ~6,842 in-game on 2026-10-07 (Raijin).
steam_reviews: 24,299 all-language, 90% positive on ~2026-10-07 (Raijin). English-only 12,212, 88% (Steam store). An earlier listing showed 15,561 positive / 1,803 negative (~90%).
implied_review_multiplier: ≥ ~82 (2,000,000 CONFIRMED units on 2026-06-04 ÷ 24,299 reviews on 2026-10-07; a lower bound, since units kept growing after June). Using VG Insights' 3.2M (Aug 18): ~130–140 [ESTIMATE].
gross_revenue: ≈ $15.9M by 2026-08-18 [ESTIMATE – VG Insights via SteamPulse; implies ~$5/unit]. Spec method: 2M CONFIRMED units × ($7.99 × 0.75 = $5.99) ≈ $12.0M by 2026-06-04; 3.2M × $5.99 ≈ $19.2M [ESTIMATE]. Chosen central ~$16M (range $12M–$19M).
net_revenue: ≈ $10.7M [ESTIMATE – $16M gross − Steam cut (30% on first $10M = $3.0M, 25% on $6M = $1.5M) = $11.5M × 0.93]. Developer/TENSTACK split unknown.
production_cost: no disclosed figure. Illustrative: 4 devs × 6–12 months × $6k/month (Sweden lean indie) ≈ $144k–$288k [ESTIMATE – dev duration NOT known; assumed]
why_popular: The shared-debt mechanic turns gambling into social drama: one bank account, so every friend's bad bet is everyone's problem; 'who gambles, when to stop' arguments; a loan-shark deadline creating 5-minute panic rounds; and 16 recognisable casino minigames (slots, roulette, etc.) with no real money. Supports up to 6 players, so it is perfect for streamer squads. The cheap $7.99 price fits multi-buying. It launched into the post-PEAK/R.E.P.O. 'friendslop' wave and gambling-meme culture.
marketing_channels: Friendslop streamer/YouTuber wave at launch (GamesRadar: 'another friendslop hit prints money on Steam'); TENSTACK collective's cross-promotion and Steam bundles with Sledding Game and How to Fish; frequent dev milestone posts (500k/600k/700k/1M/2M) that kept press coverage rolling, plus Japanese coverage (Automaton). TikTok/Next Fest/wishlists: no data.
art_style: Stylised, low-poly 3D casino tower (no detailed source found)
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: code casino minigames (slots, roulette, card games), the shared-wallet economy, timer and quota loop, item shop and Steam lobbies, and generate low-poly casino props, UI, SFX and lounge music. | AI cannot: balance the risk/reward economy so groups argue but have fun, tune 6-player chaos, run group playtests, or reproduce the TENSTACK cross-promotion network and streamer seeding. Netcode is light (turn/state-based minigames, physics-light). | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 or Godot 4 + Steam lobbies (Facepunch.Steamworks / GodotSteam) + Meshy/Tripo or casino asset packs + Midjourney/Scenario for UI + ElevenLabs SFX + Suno music.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 4–6 weeks for ~5 casino games plus a shared wallet and online lobby, ~$200–$600 (Claude Pro/Max, asset packs $50–$200, Steam Direct $100). Excludes living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 3–6 months for 15+ games, items, tower progression and 6-player stability, ~$2,000–$6,000 (tools, asset packs, freelance art/trailer, playtests, creator outreach). Excludes living costs.

data_conflicts: (1) Developer credit: TEAM GWYF (Steam) vs SkyBrave (GosuGamers) vs the four handles (GamesRadar) vs the three named devs plus contributors (TENSTACK LinkedIn). Used TEAM GWYF and ~4 core devs. (2) 500k date: May 4 vs May 5. (3) Release: May 1 vs May 2. (4) Peak CCU: 42,488 (Raijin) vs 24,666 (SteamCharts, likely stale). Chose Raijin. (5) Player cap: 1–6 (Steam) vs up to 4 (MacGamingDB). Chose 6. (6) Group A/B is borderline, because the total contributor count may exceed 5.
notes: This is part of a cluster of Swedish friendslop hits in 2026 (Sledding Game, How to Fish, Gamble With Your Friends), cross-bundled on Steam, which suggests label/collective networks (TENSTACK, Evil Landfall) matter. The rapid sequence of milestone posts (500k/600k/700k within days) was itself a marketing tactic. The theme is simulated gambling with no real money, so watch platform and age-rating policies if you build something similar.
